t: Minimum Operations to Reduce an Integer to 0 — Bit Greedy
o: We may add or subtract any power of 2 from n; minimize operations to reach 0. For n=39: +1, -8, -32 takes 3 ops. In binary, each operation flips/clears a region around one bit, so the question becomes: clear all set bits with fewest ±2^i moves. Runs of consecutive 1s are cheapest to handle by carrying: e.g., 0b111 (7) is better done as +1 then -8 (2 ops) than three subtractions.
k: Working from the lowest bit upward, a lone 1 costs one subtraction; a run of 1s of length >= 2 is cheaper to round up (add 1, causing a carry) than to subtract bit by bit.
Adding 1 to a suffix of 1s clears the whole run and sets the next bit — the classic 'carry' trick.

a.i: f(n) = 0 if n == 0; f(n) = f(n/2) if n even (just shift); otherwise f(n) = 1 + min(f(n-1), f(n+1)) — try clearing the low bit by subtracting or rounding up to create a carry. Only O(log n) distinct states exist along either branch.
s: Define f recursively as above with memoization.
a.t: O(log n) — each call halves n; memoization keeps the branching negligible.
a.sp: O(log n) — memo table and recursion depth.
